    Compute a global similarity score between two lists of authors

    compute_author_score.Rd

    Aggregates pairwise similarity scores (computed by sim_author_pair) between lists of authors, in order to produce a single score representing the degree of correspondence between the two author lists, presumably from the same bibliographic reference. The calculation mode automatically adapts depending on whether the two lists have a similar length (symmetric comparison) or very different lengths (truncation, with conditional penalization).

    Usage

    compute_author_score(
  ng,
  no,
  truncation_detected = FALSE,
  oa_large_author_threshold = .checkrefr_env$oa_large_author_threshold,
  oa_min_coverage_ratio = .checkrefr_env$oa_min_coverage_ratio,
  oa_use_window = .checkrefr_env$oa_use_window,
  oa_window_size = .checkrefr_env$oa_window_size,
  oa_sym_max_diff_abs = .checkrefr_env$oa_sym_max_diff_abs,
  oa_sym_max_diff_prop = .checkrefr_env$oa_sym_max_diff_prop,
  oa_author_lambda = .checkrefr_env$oa_author_lambda
)

    Arguments

    ng

    Character vector. Full names of the authors (extracted by Grobid for a given reference).

    no

    Character vector. Full names of the authors (returned by OpenAlex for the compared candidate).

    truncation_detected

    Logical. Indicates whether an explicit truncation marker (e.g. "et al.") was detected in the raw bibliographic reference associated with ng, typically obtained via .detect_truncation_marker(raw_reference)$detected. This parameter is only taken into account in the asymmetric case where ng is the shorter list (n_g < n_o), i.e. when the Grobid-extracted author list is itself potentially truncated. If TRUE in that situation, the coverage-based penalization is bypassed entirely and the raw score mean(pairs) is returned, regardless of the coverage value: a detected marker is taken as evidence that the shortness of ng results from an editorial convention rather than from an unreliable match, making the truncation penalty unwarranted. It has no effect in the symmetric case, in the indeterminate case, or in the mirror case where no is the shorter list. Default value: FALSE.

    oa_large_author_threshold

    Integer. Length threshold of no beyond which the indeterminate case applies when ng is very short (length(ng) <= 2). Default value: .checkrefr_env$oa_large_author_threshold (initialized to 10).

    oa_min_coverage_ratio

    Numeric between 0 and 1. Coverage threshold (min(n_g,n_o)/max(n_g,n_o)) below which the truncation penalization is not applied (see Details for reservations about this behavior). Default value: .checkrefr_env$oa_min_coverage_ratio (initialized to 0.65).

    oa_use_window

    Logical. If TRUE, enables sliding-window matching (same_position = FALSE) instead of position-by-position matching in case of truncation. Default value: .checkrefr_env$oa_use_window (initialized to FALSE).

    oa_window_size

    Integer. Half-width (in number of positions) of the sliding window used when oa_use_window = TRUE. Default value: .checkrefr_env$oa_window_size (initialized to 2).

    oa_sym_max_diff_abs

    Integer. Maximum absolute gap between length(ng) and length(no) below which the two lists are treated as symmetric. Default value: .checkrefr_env$oa_sym_max_diff_abs (initialized to 2).

    oa_sym_max_diff_prop

    Numeric between 0 and 1. Maximum relative length difference proportion tolerated for the symmetric case. Default value: .checkrefr_env$oa_sym_max_diff_prop (initialized to 0.10).

    oa_author_lambda

    Numeric. Fixed factor (independent of coverage) that modulates the intensity of the truncation penalization: score = mean(pairs) * (1 - (1 - coverage) * oa_author_lambda). Default value: .checkrefr_env$oa_author_lambda (initialized to 0.4).

    Value

    A single number (numeric) between 0 and 1 (except for rounding effects) representing the global similarity score between the two author lists:

    • 0 in the indeterminate case;

    • the average of pairwise scores in the symmetric case or in case of insufficient coverage;

    • the average of pairwise scores penalized by the factor (1 - (1 - coverage) * oa_author_lambda) in case of truncation with sufficient coverage.

    Details

    The calculation proceeds through three mutually exclusive regimes:

    1. Indeterminate case

    If length(ng) <= 2 and length(no) >= oa_large_author_threshold (default 10), the comparison is deemed unreliable (too few Grobid authors against a very long OpenAlex list) and the function returns 0 without further calculation.

    2. Symmetric case

    The two lists are treated as "of comparable length" if: $$|n_g - n_o| \le \code{oa\_sym\_max\_diff\_abs}$$ or $$\frac{\min(n_g, n_o)}{\max(n_g, n_o)} \ge 1 - \code{oa\_sym\_max\_diff\_prop}$$ with \(n_g = length(ng)\), \(n_o = length(no)\), and by default oa_sym_max_diff_abs = 2, oa_sym_max_diff_prop = 0.10. Note that as soon as n_g == n_o, this condition is automatically true (zero gap), so this case systematically covers lists of the same length. The \(n = \min(n_g, n_o)\) first authors of each list are then compared term by term with sim_author_pair(ng[i], no[i], same_position = TRUE), and the final score is their arithmetic mean: $$score = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} sim\_author\_pair(ng_i, no_i)$$

    3. Asymmetric case (truncation of one of the two lists)

    If the lists are deemed too different in length for the symmetric case, a coverage rate is calculated: $$coverage = \min(n_g, n_o) / \max(n_g, n_o)$$ Two matching strategies for the min(n_g, n_o) authors of the shorter list are possible:

    • oa_use_window = FALSE (default): direct matching position by position, sim_author_pair(..., same_position = TRUE).

    • oa_use_window = TRUE: for each author \(i\) of the shorter list, the best score is retained among the authors of the longer list located within a window of \(\pm\) oa_window_size positions (default 2) around rank \(i\), using sim_author_pair(..., same_position = FALSE) (F1-type score, consistent with the lack of strict positional alignment induced by the window).

    A multiplicative penalization is then applied only if coverage remains sufficient (coverage >= oa_min_coverage_ratio, default 0.65): $$\lambda_{cov} = 1 - coverage$$ $$score = mean(pairs) \times (1 - \lambda_{cov} \times \code{oa\_author\_lambda})$$ where oa_author_lambda (default 0.4) is a fixed factor that modulates the intensity of the penalization related to truncation: the lower the coverage (thus the higher \(\lambda_{cov}\)), the more the average score is reduced, proportionally to oa_author_lambda.

    In case of insufficient coverage (coverage < oa_min_coverage_ratio), no penalization is applied and the raw score mean(pairs) is returned as is. This design choice is motivated by the fact that author lists extracted from bibliographic references (parameter ng) are structurally limited by citation norms (truncation via "et al." beyond a few authors), while lists from OpenAlex (no) tend to be exhaustive. Very low coverage in the n_g < n_o case could therefore reflect a bibliographic format artifact rather than genuine matching uncertainty.

    See also

    sim_author_pair for the underlying pairwise similarity calculation.

    Examples

    # Symmetric case: lists of the same length
ng <- c("Jean Dupont", "Marie Curie")
no <- c("J. Dupont", "M. Curie")
compute_author_score(ng, no)
#> [1] 1

# Slight truncation with sufficient coverage (0.67 >= 0.65) -> penalized
ng2 <- c("Jean Dupont", "Marie Curie", "Paul Martin")
no2 <- c("J. Dupont", "M. Curie")
compute_author_score(ng2, no2)
#> [1] 1

# Severe truncation with insufficient coverage -> no penalization
ng3 <- c("Jean Dupont", "Marie Curie", "Paul Martin", "Alice Bernard")
no3 <- c("J. Dupont")
compute_author_score(ng3, no3)
#> [1] 1

# Using the sliding-window mode for matching
compute_author_score(ng2, no2, oa_use_window = TRUE, oa_window_size = 1)
#> [1] 1
